steps.name: Normalize counts and build per-sample signature score
steps.question: After normalizing the 12000 x 121 raw Salmon gene counts (variance-stabilizing/log-CPM normalization), what is each of the 120 samples' expression-based score for the 20-gene signature (signature_genes.csv, unweighted — no weights supplied)?

grounding.reason: No knowledge_recommend tool attached in this session; standard VST + unweighted signature scoring is a routine bulk RNA-seq preprocessing choice given no signature weights are supplied.

acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix loaded and confirmed as 12000 genes x 120 samples (excluding the gene-symbol column) matching the 120-row metadata table by sample ID
All 20 signature genes are located in the count matrix gene symbols; any missing genes are reported explicitly by name, not silently dropped without note
Normalization method stated explicitly (e.g., DESeq2 VST or log2(CPM+1)) and applied before scoring

A single unweighted per-sample signature score is produced (e.g., mean of z-scored normalized expression across the 20 genes, or an unweighted ssGSEA/singscore) and written out as one score per sample keyed to sample ID
Output table joins score to metadata (condition, time, event) for all 120 samples with no sample dropped silently

steps.name: Cox PH: signature score vs time-to-event adjusting for case/control
steps.question: Does the 20-gene signature score associate with time to event (time, event columns in metadata.csv) in a Cox proportional-hazards model that adjusts for case vs control status, across the 60 cases and 60 controls?

grounding.reason: Standard prognostic-association Cox modeling adjusted for a known covariate; no knowledge_recommend tool attached to ground against a house rule.

acceptance_criteria: Cox model fit as time/event ~ signature_score + condition(case/control) on all 120 samples with available time/event data; sample size used in the fit is reported
Hazard ratio, 95% CI, and p-value reported for the signature score term specifically (independent of condition)
Hazard ratio, 95% CI, and p-value reported for the condition (case vs control) term
Proportional-hazards assumption checked (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals) and any violation reported explicitly rather than ignored
A model with a score-by-condition interaction term is also fit and reported to assess whether the score-outcome association differs between cases and controls
Association between signature score and condition (case vs control) itself is reported (e.g., t-test/Wilcoxon) to flag potential collinearity between the score and the adjustment covariate
Concordance index (C-index) or equivalent goodness-of-fit reported for the adjusted model

plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs survival adjusting for case/control
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort is 60 cases vs 60 controls (121 columns = gene column + 120 samples matching 120 metadata rows) with raw Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 121), a 20-gene signature list with no weights, and a metadata table carrying condition, time, and event. The question is whether a per-sample score built from the 20-gene signature associates with time-to-event after adjusting for case/control status. This requires: (1) standard bulk RNA-seq normalization of the raw counts (library-size/variance-stabilizing normalization, since raw integer counts cannot be used directly in a linear/Cox score without normalization), (2) construction of a per-sample signature score from the 20 genes (since no weights are supplied, an unweighted approach such as mean of normalized/scaled expression, or ssGSEA/singscore, is appropriate — done in the bulk-transcriptomics-agent to keep it tied to the expression matrix), (3) a Cox proportional-hazards model regressing time-to-event on the signature score with case/control status as a covariate, testing the score's independent association, including PH assumption diagnostics, and (4) a sensitivity/robustness step examining whether the score-outcome association differs by case/control (interaction term) and whether the signature score itself differs between cases and controls (to flag potential collinearity/confounding). No enrichment, immune-deconvolution or drug-repurposing steps are added because the question is purely a signature-score-survival association question, not a discovery or mechanistic question.
